what_its_for: Valganciclovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat or prevent a viral infection called cytomegalovirus (CMV). CMV can cause serious eye problems (CMV retinitis) in people with HIV/AIDS, and it can also cause problems in people who have received an organ transplant. This medicine helps keep the virus under control so it does not damage your organs or vision.
how_to_take: Take valganciclovir by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Always take it WITH food — this helps your body absorb the medicine properly and can reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablets whole. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablets. If you are using the liquid (oral solution), shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with the measuring device provided. Wash your hands before and after handling the medication.
dosing: Your dose depends on your condition, kidney function, and body weight (for children). For adults treating CMV retinitis, the usual starting dose is 900 mg (two 450 mg tablets) twice a day for 21 days, then 900 mg once a day. For preventing CMV after a transplant, the usual dose is 900 mg once a day. Your doctor will calculate the right dose for you. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day or almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store valganciclovir tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them in a dry place away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. The liquid oral solution should be stored in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C) — do NOT freeze it. The liquid should be used within 49 days of being prepared. Keep all forms of this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused medication safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid handling crushed or broken tablets — the powder can be harmful if it touches your skin or eyes. If contact occurs, wash the area thoroughly with soap and water. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, confused, or uncoordinated, as this medicine can affect your ability to do these tasks safely. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child while taking this medicine — it can cause serious birth defects. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period of time after stopping (ask your doctor how long). Avoid breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Avoid live vaccines unless your doctor approves them. Limit alcohol as it may worsen side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: unusual bruising or bleeding, signs of low blood counts such as fever, chills, or frequent infections, extreme tiredness or weakness, pale or yellowish skin, severe stomach pain, blood in your urine or stool, seizures, confusion or hallucinations, severe headache, changes in your vision, or signs of kidney problems such as very little urination or swelling in your legs or feet. Also tell your doctor if you are planning to get pregnant or if you think you may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Valganciclovir does not cure CMV, but it helps control the virus. For CMV retinitis, you may start to notice some improvement in symptoms within a few weeks, but it may take longer for your eye condition to stabilize. For transplant patients, the medicine works in the background to prevent CMV from becoming active. It is very important to keep taking this medicine even if you feel well, because stopping too soon can allow the virus to grow and become harder to treat.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor will adjust your dose if your kidneys are not working well. Tell your doctor about any kidney issues before starting this medicine. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially kidney-related ones, and may need closer monitoring. Children: Doses in children are calculated based on body size. The liquid form is often used for children. Pregnancy: This medicine can cause birth defects and should NOT be used during pregnancy unless absolutely necessary. Women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 30 days after the last dose. Men should use condoms during treatment and for at least 90 days after the last dose. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine, as it may pass into breast milk and harm the baby.
